method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the writing-l4-rules skill; the steps with deadlines in s 42(3), s 73(2)(a) and Rules s 15(2) are regulative rules (PARTY ... DO/MUST ... WITHIN ... LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE) run inside plain-fact questions; no REFUSE (gaps answer `not covered` or NOTHING, asserted); every consideration, satisfaction or determination of the Operator or the reviewer asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. First encoding of this Act. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: National Redress Scheme for Institutional Child Sexual Abuse Act 2018, No. 45, 2018, Compilation No. 9, compilation date 2024-09-28 (register id C2024C00613; Federal Register of Legislation, retrieved 2026-10-13), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2018A00045.txt, with the s 30(2) formula from C2018A00045.formulas.md. scope: From the survivor's seat: ss 6 (definitions used), 12-17, 19-22, 24(4), (7), 26(1), 28, 29(1)-(3), 30, 31(2), 34(4)-(10), 37, 40, 42, 43, 45, 48(1D), 49, 50, 51(2)-(3), 52, 53, 54, 56B-56D, 58-61, 63, 64, 73, 75(4), 76(3), 78, 167, 193(1); Rules ss 4B, 6, 11, 12, 15, 26(3)-(5), 33(3). Out: Chapter 1 and Part 2-1; notices to institutions and funders of last resort; cost sharing among institutions and funders of last resort (s 29(2)(b)-(m), s 31(3), Rules ss 19-29A, whose formulas the Rules deposit lost); revocation (s 29(4)-(7)); the frameworks (ss 32, 33, 55, 56); payment administration; the special assessment procedure (s 63(3)-(8)); security notices (ss 65-71); Part 3-3 reassessment; review procedure; Parts 4-2, 4-3; Chapters 5, 6 (except s 167), 7 (except s 193), 8; Rules ss 8-10.
seat: the survivor (a person sexually abused as a child in circumstances for which an institution is responsible, who applies for redress, receives an offer, accepts or declines it, and may seek review; in ss 58-60, the person asking what happens to the redress payment when the applicant dies before accepting)
